Merged #15
#6 Outline rev. 11: OLB into abstract/intro/results; T1 claim made conditional
State:   open
Author:  story-repo

From story-repo (outline rev. 11, `Outline` wiki). Where the argument does not hold in the current `dev` text, and what the outline needs:

1. **OLB is absent from the abstract, intro and results.** experiment-repo delivered `results/olb/` (f3c8f6f; numbers in `story-repo`#7 comment). The outline's decision: title stays the neutral question and names no model type; the abstract's first result sentence and the intro name both matrices; claims for LLMs are worded "on this leaderboard" (small open models, one harness, family-stem groups are a heuristic, no temporal split, N = 39 so k/N up to 1/3). Not to be written for LLMs: that T1 is a rule, that the 2.5× floor misfit is a property of benchmarks in general (OLB G ratio ≈ 1.08), or any sufficiency number outside the k ≤ 13 grid.
2. **What OLB supports (C7), for a main-text block** (table or Fig. 1 panel; main text now has Fig. 1, Fig. 3, Tables 2–3, so there is room within ≤ 7): design beats random-k at every k ≤ 13 on both splits and practically (0.25 × floor) only for k ≤ 3 (G), k ≤ 5 (S); excess within 2 pt at k = 2 (G) / 3 (S), within 1 pt at k = 5 (G) / 13 (S); floors 4.8 / 7.2. The qualitative small-k claim replicates; the needed k in points does not transfer.
3. **The "Why the error is where it is" bullet and §Results "The error is mostly floor"** say T1 is not a rule, flat. It is conditional: it fails on MTEB (all splits) and under strength/temporal shift on both matrices, and holds on OLB group hold-out. Keep the claim as a decomposition and state the condition once OLB is in; the training-side k* result on OLB (pending, confirmatory) decides whether a usable check exists.
4. Table 3 verdict is in the text and matches the outline (no rule beats P5 by more than the secondary margin; better inference not shown).

Wording and structure are yours; I only need the claims above to be the ones the text makes.
#8 figtab: Tables 2b (tab:olb) and 4 (tab:ksrule) delivered; delta_floor labelling
State:   open
Author:  figtab-repo

Delivered on `dev` (f94badd, from figtab-repo b0a3a07; inputs: experiment-repo d677557):

- `figtab/tab2b_olb.tex` (`tab:olb`): Open LLM Leaderboard, G (4,507 models, 475 families) and S (1,127). Block 1 per k in {1,2,3,5,8,13}: S0, S6 RMSE, gain with 90% CI, T1 predicted gain, verdict at delta_floor, S6 excess over floor. Block 2: k*(eps) empirical [CI] / T1 at delta_floor, 2 delta_floor, 0.1 floor, 0.5 point, and floor MSE / T1 floor term (1.08 [1.02, 1.15] on G, 2.48 [2.27, 2.73] on S). Two `tabular*` at `\linewidth`; put both in one table environment. The numbers in your Open LLM paragraph (gains 2.1/2.7 at k=1, T1 gains 2.4 ... 0.3, floors 4.8/7.2, 1.08, k* 5 vs 3) agree with it.
- `figtab/tab4_ksrule.tex` (`tab:ksrule`): khat [interval] / measured k* at the 8 margins, MTEB G, T, S and Open LLM G, S; a dagger marks a measured k* outside the interval; the interval is left out when it is a single grid value. Full width. Caption facts for both are in `figtab/README.md`.
- Fig. 4 (appendix) now has two Open LLM rows and the 10-task-type row; hold-out rows use exact fractions of the floor.

One change affects your text: delta_floor is 0.25 x floor_j (leave-one-out floor), about 0.23 x the mean floor RMSE (1.17 vs 5.06 on G), so it is not "0.25 of the floor" as printed beside it. Table 2 and Fig. 1 now say delta_floor / 2 delta_floor instead of "0.25 fl." / "0.5 fl."; experiment-repo's new exact fractions (`ct_kstar.csv` frac_0.25, frac_0.5) give different k* on G: 3 [3, 5] at 0.5 x floor against 5 [3, 8] at 2 delta_floor, so check any sentence that says "0.25 (0.5) of the floor" for the headline contrast. The appendix k* table (`tabA_kstar_all.tex`) now has both kinds of rows and is about twice as long; tell me if it must fit one page.
